title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction
title_zh: 遗传耦合花蜜奖励与信号，支撑传粉者吸引
abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.
abstract_zh: 动物传粉者支撑生物多样性与全球农业，但协调花蜜奖励与信号以吸引传粉者的分子机制仍知之甚少。通过对瓜类遗传多样性的表型分析，我们鉴定出花蜜缺失1 (nls1)，其编码YABBY家族转录因子YABBY5 (YAB5)，作为整合传粉者吸引性状的核心调节因子。YAB5在花蜜腺发育初期与CRABS CLAW (CRC)相互作用，通过抑制替代花器官命运来指定花蜜腺身份。随着花朵成熟，YAB5直接激活4-α-葡萄糖转移酶2 (DPE2)，促进淀粉重新分配，这对花蜜分泌是必需的；同时促进花瓣生长与花舒展。在花瓣中，YAB5直接结合MYB111依赖的黄酮合成途径，产生紫外线花蜜导向条纹，并间接影响花挥发物的释放。破坏YAB5、DPE2或MYB111会降低传粉者访问频率。综上所述，这些研究揭示了发育调节因子如何将器官谱系与器官特异性代谢程序耦合，在花蕾期同步花蜜奖励与信号的产生。
